Built from published figures

Bore and stroke (102 × 120 mm, 5.9 L), the firing order, the clockwise turn seen from the front and the connecting-rod length. The crank, rods and pistons move from those numbers alone, so the strokes, the 120° firing interval and the piston heights are exact.

Estimated

When each valve opens and closes. It is worked out from the stock 12-valve cam figures Colt Cams lists (duration 159° intake and 204° exhaust, lobe lift 0.235 and 0.263 in, lobe separation 102°). The listing does not say where the duration is measured, so I took the usual 0.050 in figure, gave each lobe a smooth modelled shape and assumed a 1.5:1 rocker ratio. Valve lash is left out of the motion. Read the timing as a good estimate, not a spec.

The glow in each piston bowl is a stylised gas-pressure trace from the same crank geometry and the 6BT’s 17.5:1 compression ratio. It builds through compression, peaks near top dead centre (where the head hides the bowl), fades as the gas expands and ends when the exhaust valve opens.

Drawn to proportion, not measured

The casting, the head and the valve train, with one rocker on its own post for each valve. The front gear train is a sketch of the real idea: the cam gear turns the same way as the crank at half its speed, but tooth counts and sizes are made up, and the pump and accessory gears are left out. The pointer under the damper reads its degree scale: zero, the mark with the dot beside it, stands at the pointer when cylinder 1 is at firing top dead centre. The mark on the flywheel rim points the same way as the first throw. The bolts, core plugs, dowels, pan ribs, drain plug, lift bracket, and the oil with its pickup tube in the pan, are drawn in a plausible pattern, not copied from a part drawing.

Not drawn

The camshaft and tappets inside the block, the manifolds, the turbocharger, the injection pump and the oil and water pumps. I assumed the 1994–98 12-valve engine with the P7100 inline pump and a Holset turbo; the pump and turbo sit on sides of the engine that are cut away or not drawn.
